name: Status update
description: Tells someone a long-running job, review or request has moved, which state it is in now, and where that state sits in the sequence.

origin.note: Design: progress — a tinted status strip, then the sequence on a ruled rail with the current stage numbered.

subject: {{ item_name }} — {{ state_label }}
preheader: Where this sits in the sequence, and when the next change is expected.

item_name.description: What moved, named the way the recipient would name it rather than as an internal job id. It leads the subject line, so a queue name beats a UUID.

state_label.description: The state it is in right now, in one or two words. This is the fact the recipient opened the email for, so it also carries the subject line.

headline.description: One line saying what actually changed. Written as a statement about the work, not about the email — 'Compiling 48,000 records', not 'Your request has been updated'.

position_text.description: Where the current state sits in the run, so the reader can tell a long wait from a nearly-finished one. Leave empty for workflows with no fixed number of stages.

summary.description: A sentence or two on what this state means for the recipient — whether they need to do anything, and what happens without them.
summary.example: Nothing is needed from you while this runs. We will send one more email when the file is ready to download.

stages_heading.description: Heading over the sequence, so the numbered list is read as a route rather than as instructions.

stages.description: The full sequence as `text` (the stage) and `detail` (what happened at it, or that it has not started). Listing the stages already passed is what turns a status into a position.

reference_label.description: Label for the reference row. Say what support will ask for, e.g. 'Job reference' or 'Ticket'.

reference.description: The identifier a support conversation will start from. Set in the mono face so a long id can be read aloud a character at a time.

eta_label.description: Lead-in for the expectation line, changed to suit the workflow — 'Expected to finish', 'Decision expected by'.

eta_value.description: When the next change is expected, stated with a timezone if it is a clock time. Leave empty rather than guessing; an absent estimate reads better than one that slips.

action_url.description: Where the recipient can watch this themselves instead of waiting for the next email.

button_label.description: Label for the action. Name the destination, not the verb — 'Open the export', not 'Click here'.

footer_text.description: The closing line. Says how often these go out, which is what stops a status email from feeling like noise.
footer_text.default: You get one of these each time the state changes, and nothing in between.
